hook.line: Hernando can name the year he first walked into Rosa's café, but most of us just count back from today: two weeks ago, forty years ago. Spanish counts back too, only it puts the ago word first.
hook.es: Vine a Bogotá hace una semana.
hook.en: I came to Bogotá a week ago.

examples.es: Hablé con mi mamá hace cinco minutos.
examples.en: I talked to my mom five minutes ago.

examples.es: Hernando vino al café hace cuarenta y siete años.
examples.en: Hernando came to the café forty-seven years ago.

examples.es: Compramos la máquina hace diez años.
examples.en: We bought the machine ten years ago.

examples.es: Hace dos días vi a Mariana en la esquina.
examples.en: Two days ago I saw Mariana on the corner.
How long ago did you arrive? (to a friend)

examples.es: No fue hace un año, fue hace dos.
examples.en: It wasn't a year ago, it was two.

rule:
English puts ago after the time: two days ago. Spanish puts *hace* in front of it: *hace dos días*.

*Hace* never changes. It's *hace un minuto*, *hace una hora*, *hace cuarenta años*, whoever did the thing and however much time it was.

Because it points at a moment that is over, the verb next to it is in the past: *llegó*, *vino*, *compramos*.

The *hace* chunk can sit at the end or at the start: *Vi a Mariana hace dos días* or *Hace dos días vi a Mariana*. Same meaning.

To ask how long ago, use *¿Hace cuánto…?*: *¿Hace cuánto llegaste?*

One thing *hace* is not: before. *Antes* means earlier or before; *hace* means counted back from right now.
smallPrint: *Hace* is really the verb *hacer* (to make, to do): *hace dos años* is literally something like it makes two years. Grammar books file it under time expressions with *hacer*.

options: Vale arrived an hour ago.
Vale arrived an hour late.
Vale arrives in an hour.
They arrived three days ago.
We arrived three days ago.
We're arriving in three days.

readAndPick.es: Hace un mes vi a Mariana.
options: I'm going to see Mariana in a month.
I see Mariana every month.
I saw Mariana a month ago.
How long ago did you arrive?
How long are you staying?
When are you arriving?

readAndPick.es: Compraron la radio hace veinte años.
options: We bought the radio twenty years ago.
They bought the radio twenty years ago.
They've had the radio for twenty years.
Hernando comes every week.
Hernando is coming in a week.
Hernando came a week ago.

readAndPick.es: Cerraron la panadería hace dos años.
options: They closed the bakery two years ago.
They're closing the bakery in two years.
We closed the bakery two years ago.

readAndPick.es: Hace diez minutos abrí la puerta.
options: He opened the door ten minutes ago.
I opened the door ten minutes ago.
I opened the door for ten minutes.

readAndPick.es: Pusieron el letrero hace un mes.
options: They're putting up the sign next month.
I put up the sign a month ago.
They put up the sign a month ago.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Vale llegó ___ una hora.* (*hace* or *antes*) Vale arrived an hour ago.
yourTurn.why: Ago, counted back from now, is *hace*, and it goes before the time.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Hernando ___ hace dos días.* (*vino* or *viene*) Hernando came two days ago.
yourTurn.why: *Hace* points at a finished moment, so the verb is in the past: *vino*.

yourTurn.prompt: I talked to my mom five minutes ago.
yourTurn.answer: Hablé con mi mamá hace cinco minutos.
accept: Hace cinco minutos hablé con mi mamá.
Hablé con mi mamá hace 5 minutos.
yourTurn.why: Past verb, then *hace* and the time: *hace cinco minutos*.

yourTurn.prompt: We bought the machine ten years ago.
yourTurn.answer: Compramos la máquina hace diez años.
accept: Hace diez años compramos la máquina.
yourTurn.why: *Hace* stays the same with years, hours or minutes.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: How long ago did you arrive?
yourTurn.why: How long ago is *¿Hace cuánto…?*, and to a friend you arrived is *llegaste*.

yourTurn.prompt: Move the time to the front: *Vi a Mariana hace dos días.*
yourTurn.answer: Hace dos días vi a Mariana.
yourTurn.why: The *hace* chunk can open the sentence, and the meaning stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about they: *Volví hace un año.*
yourTurn.why: Only the verb changes; *hace un año* never does.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English says the time and then ago; Spanish says *hace* first, then the time.
Close. *Antes* means before or earlier; for ago, counted back from now, use *hace*.
*Hace* points at a moment that is over, so the verb goes in the past: *llegó*.

pitfalls.wrong: Compramos la máquina hacen diez años.
pitfalls.right: Compramos la máquina hace diez años.
pitfalls.why: Nearly. *Hace* doesn't turn plural with years; it's always *hace*.

personal: Write two true things with *hace*: when you started learning Spanish, and the last time you ate something really good.
